messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: problem with cmdstan develop
parts:
Good news is that the release works as expected.

In the develop version, everything compiels fine for the model,
then I get this:

~/cmdstan(develop)$ make ~/temp2/idx

--- Translating Stan model to C++ code ---
bin/stanc /Users/carp/temp2/idx.stan --o=/Users/carp/temp2/idx.hpp
Model name=idx_model
Input file=/Users/carp/temp2/idx.stan
Output file=/Users/carp/temp2/idx.hpp
make: *** [/Users/carp/temp2/idx.hpp] Segmentation fault: 11


Oddly, I get a different behavior when I run it immediately again:

~/cmdstan(develop)$ make ~/temp2/idx

--- Linking C++ model ---
clang++ -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -I src -I stan/src -isystem stan/lib/stan_math/ -isystem stan/lib/stan_math/lib/eigen_3.2.4 -isystem stan/lib/stan_math/lib/boost_1.58.0 -Wall -pipe -DEIGEN_NO_DEBUG -Wno-unused-function -ftemplate-depth-256 -O0 -o /Users/carp/temp2/idx src/cmdstan/main.cpp -include /Users/carp/temp2/idx.hpp
src/cmdstan/main.cpp:7:36: error: use of undeclared identifier 'stan_model'
return stan::services::command<stan_model>(argc,argv);
^
1 error generated.
make: *** [/Users/carp/temp2/idx] Error 1



And here's my state of git and submodules:

~/cmdstan(develop)$ git status
# On branch develop
# Your branch is ahead of 'origin/develop' by 3 commits.
# (use "git push" to publish your local commits)
#
nothing to commit, working directory clean

~/cmdstan(develop)$ make stan-revert
git submodule update --init --recursive
~/cmdstan(develop)$ cd stan/
~/cmdstan/stan((6796c99...))$

~/cmdstan/stan((6796c99...))$ make math-revert
git submodule update --init --recursive
~/cmdstan/stan/lib/stan_math((a412ebb...))$

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] problem with cmdstan develop
parts:
Bob, I can't reproduce on my end.

Can you try:

cd ~/cmdstan
make clean-all
rm ~/temp2/idx ~/temp2/idx.hpp
make ~/temp2/idx


Also, I'm assuming the three commits to develop are merge bubbles. If you can verify that's correct, maybe you'd want to get back to the state of develop?

git reset --hard origin/develop



Can you let me know if those set of instructions work? I'm not seeing the problem on my end. Maybe there's something with idx.stan?
